title: Classifying an uploaded receipt PDF
scenario: ReceiptWise, a personal expense tracker, sends each uploaded PDF to a vision model that returns a document type code, a confidence tier, and a language code so the app can file it correctly.

content.text:
Classify the attached PDF for our expense tracker.

Return JSON only, no other text, with exactly these keys:
- source_document_type_code: one of "inv" (invoice), "rcp" (receipt), "qte" (quote), "po" (purchase order), "oth" (other)
- extraction_confidence_tier: one of "high", "med", "low", "none"
- language: ISO 639-1 two-letter code for the document's primary language

How to tell the codes apart:
- "inv": has an invoice number, a due date, and a bill-to section, even if the vendor also calls it something else on the page.
- "rcp": already marked paid, usually from a point-of-sale system, with a shorter itemized list and a payment method printed near the total.
- "qte": explicitly says "quote" or "estimate" and has no due date, since nothing has been billed yet.
- "po": issued by the buyer rather than the seller, referencing a vendor and a delivery address rather than a bill-to address.
- "oth": anything that does not clearly match one of the above, including contracts, statements, and delivery notes.

Confidence tier guidance:
- "high": every field above is clearly printed and unambiguous, and the file is a clean digital export rather than a scan.
- "med": the fields are present but partly handwritten, faint, or on a scanned photo rather than a digital export.
- "low": some required fields are missing or only partially legible.
- "none": use only if the file is unreadable, corrupted, or blank; do not use it just because you are unsure of the document type.

If the document is a scanned photo rather than a clean PDF export, prefer "med" over "high" even when the text looks fully legible, since totals on a scan can still be misread by a downstream parser.

Do not guess a document type if the page has no visible vendor name, line items, or total; return "oth" in that case rather than picking the closest-sounding option.
